# Introduction

Two chapters exercise the modern conservation-genomics toolkit on public whole-genome data: (1) the
new Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) genetic-diversity indicators applied to the endangered green
peafowl (*Pavo muticus*), and (2) realized-versus-masked genetic load in the inbred Scandinavian wolf
(*Canis lupus*). The cross-cutting question is not "what is the number?" but **"how fragile is the
verdict to defensible analyst choices?"** — filtering stringency, whether population structure is
modelled, the GERP threshold that defines a deleterious site, and the run-of-homozygosity length that
counts as inbreeding. Where a headline moves under choices a competent analyst could each justify, we
report the movement itself as the result.

The GBF adopted a genetic-diversity target — the proportion of populations with effective size
$N_e > 500$ [@hoban2020; @mastretta2024] — that is now being operationalized by national reporters. A
central practical question is how stable that indicator is when computed from real, small-sample data.
The wolf chapter provides a contrasting, data-rich case where the source study [@smeds2022] published a
per-individual load table we can reproduce exactly, letting us separate genuine signal from analyst
sensitivity.

# Methods

## Data

- **Green peafowl** — @dong2021, Dryad `10.5061/dryad.ffbg79ctc`. Modern resequencing across three
  regional populations plus six museum specimens. After a kinship screen (below) the analysis set is
  **`{python} R.peafowl_n` unrelated individuals** across **`{python} R.population_n`**;
  Cambodia (n = 1) is dropped. A separate museum-versus-modern comparative callset supports the
  temporal-erosion angle (`{python} R.museum_n` museum and `{python} R.modern_temporal_n` modern
  individuals after comparative-sample QC).
- **Scandinavian wolf** — @smeds2022, Dryad `10.5061/dryad.7m0cfxpzj`. `{python} R.wolf_n` individuals with
  ancestral-allele-polarized SNPs (`INFO/AA`, two outgroups), VEP/SIFT coding annotation, and
  per-site GERP conservation scores. Individuals carry a time-period label (founding cohort ~1983
  through 2007–2014) plus outbred references (Finland, Russia, immigrants).

All analyses start from the deposited VCFs (no re-calling from reads); every threshold lives in
`config/config.yaml`, and the fragility axes *are* that config made executable.

## QC and filtering (peafowl)

Two callsets are derived from a shared normalized parent (`bcftools norm -m -any`, biallelic SNPs on
the 32 autosomes): **unpruned Set A** (neutral) feeds currentNe2, while an **LD-pruned derivative of
Set A** feeds the structure analyses; **Set B** (lightly filtered, no MAF/MAC/HWE/LD-prune) feeds
diversity and preserves rare alleles. The *filtering-stringency*
knob re-derives Set A per preset — **lenient / standard / strict** (max-missing 0.7/0.8/0.9,
min-GQ 15/20/30, min-DP 4/6/8, MAC 3) — yielding **`{python} R.postmac_counts`** post-MAC sites
(a ~`{python} R.filter_spread`× spread). Per-population HWE ($P < 10^{-6}$ in any population) is applied to avoid Wahlund
false departures. A confirmatory KING kinship screen retains all `{python} R.peafowl_n` individuals.

## Contemporary $N_e$ and the fragility cube (peafowl)

The parameter sweep is `{filter} × {structure}` → `results/cube/results_cube.parquet`, with
**currentNe2** as the sole automated estimator. LD-based $N_e$ estimators read $N_e$ *out of* linkage
disequilibrium, so the un-pruned Set A is fed with a genome size of 32 Morgans (the autosome count),
invoking currentNe2's cross-chromosome ("no genetic map needed") mode [@santiago2024]; LD-pruning
would destroy the very signal being measured. The *structure* knob contrasts **modelled**
(`per_population`, the three values feeding the GBF fraction) with **ignored** (`pooled`, all 22
lumped — a Wahlund-biased cautionary contrast). NeEstimator-LDNe is a manual field-standard
cross-check outside the DAG; **GONE2** provides a recent-trajectory *context* panel only (a borrowed
avian recombination rate, macrochromosomes only), never the contemporary indicator [@waples2024].

## GBF indicators (peafowl)

From the cube we compute the **$N_e > 500$ indicator** (proportion of per-population estimates above
threshold, per preset) and a **robustness** table (verdict stability across presets). The
complementary **Populations Maintained (PM)** indicator is non-genomic, curated from IUCN/BirdLife
range records at country resolution; a census $N_c$ proxy contrast uses a conservative vertebrate
$N_e{:}N_c = 0.1$ [@frankham]. The three-state verdict — pass / fail / **indeterminate** (CI straddles
500, or no convergence) — is precomputed in the workflow.

## Genetic load and ROH (wolf)

Per-individual load faithfully re-implements @smeds2022's `gerp_load_polarized.py`. For each SNP the
derived allele is the non-ancestral allele (`INFO/AA`); a site is **deleterious** at threshold $t$ if
its GERP RS score $> t$. Per individual we accumulate, in a single per-chromosome VCF stream,
GERP-weighted **realized** load ($\sum 2g$ over homozygous-derived deleterious sites $/$ calls) and
**masked** load ($\sum g$ over heterozygous deleterious sites $/$ calls), summing raw counts across
chromosomes. We extend the source method by sweeping the GERP threshold over **{2, 3, 4}** in one pass
— the wolf-side fragility knob — while GERP > 4 reproduces the deposit's precomputed table exactly
(Results). Runs of homozygosity are called with `bcftools roh` (GT-based HMM, a documented constant
recombination rate) and summarized as per-individual $F_{ROH}$ swept over a ROH-length cutoff, with
long ROH ($\geq 1.5$ Mb) read as recent inbreeding [@bertorelle2022].

# Results

## Peafowl: diversity, structure, and temporal contrast

PCA cleanly separates the three populations (minimum centroid gap `{python} f"{R.pca_gap:.1f}"`
versus maximum within-population spread `{python} f"{R.pca_within:.1f}"`), though per-axis variance
is low (PC1 ≈ `{python} f"{R.pc1_variance:.1f}"`%) and ADMIXTURE cross-validation favours
$K$ = `{python} R.admixture_best_k` — a small-$n$ artefact, so structure is read from PCA rather than
a "best $K$". Thailand is least diverse (expected heterozygosity
`{python} f"{R.thailand_he:.3f}"`; rarefied allelic richness `{python} f"{R.thailand_ar:.2f}"`), and
Yunnan shows a heterozygote deficit ($F_{IS}$ = `{python} f"{R.yunnan_fis:.3f}"`) consistent with elevated within-population
relatedness. The museum-versus-modern temporal contrast (angle G) is **weak and metric-dependent**:
median $\pi$ and $H_o$ are marginally higher in museum specimens (erosion-consistent), but $H_e$ and
rarefied allelic richness are essentially flat. We report a direction, not an erosion claim, with
aDNA-deamination and geographic-mismatch caveats.

![Peafowl population structure on the first two PCA axes, computed from the LD-pruned derivative of
Set A. Separation supports population-aware analysis, while low per-axis variance and small sample
sizes limit how strongly the geometry should be interpreted.](../results/figures/pca.png){#fig-pca
fig-alt="Scatterplot of peafowl samples on PCA axes one and two, coloured by population." width="90%"}

## Peafowl: contemporary $N_e$ and the fragility of the GBF verdict

**No population confidently passes $N_e > 500$ under any filtering preset** (`{python} R.ne_pass_by_preset`
pass for lenient / standard / strict). Verdicts are *fail* (point and 90% CI below 500) or
*indeterminate*. Under the lenient preset the cross-chromosome estimates are Yunnan
`{python} R.ne_yunnan`, Thailand `{python} R.ne_thailand`, and Vietnam `{python} R.ne_vietnam` —
the lone point above 500, but with a CI straddling it, hence
*indeterminate*, not a pass. Under stricter presets several per-population estimates fail to converge
(extreme heterozygote excess at small $n$), so convergence itself is preset-fragile (Table:
`results/tables/gbf_robustness.tsv`). Pooling across populations (structure ignored) trends low and
rises with stringency (`{python} R.pooled_ne`), below most per-population estimates — the predicted Wahlund
direction, muddied by small-$n$ noise.

The result is therefore two-sided: the **headline is robust** (`{python} R.ne_headline` pass regardless of preset), while
the **underlying estimates are fragile** (`{python} R.unstable_population_count`/`{python} R.population_count`
populations change verdict across presets; Vietnam is
estimable under lenient but not under stricter filters). The GONE2 context trajectory shows a recent
decline (approximately `{python} f"{R.gone_old:,.0f}"` → `{python} f"{R.gone_recent:,.0f}"`
over ~`{python} R.gone_generations` generations), consistent with an endangered
species but presented as context only.

![Contemporary peafowl effective-size estimates across filtering presets and population-structure
treatments. The horizontal threshold marks $N_e=500$; wide intervals and non-converged cells show
why the estimate magnitudes are fragile even though the no-confident-pass headline is stable. Only
the per-population cells feed the GBF indicator.](../results/figures/ne_cube.png){#fig-ne-cube
fig-alt="Point and interval plot of currentNe2 estimates across filters and structure treatments, with a threshold at 500." width="90%"}

## Peafowl: the two GBF indicators disagree

The genomic indicator gives **`{python} R.ne_headline` populations $N_e$-secure**, whereas **Populations Maintained =
`{python} R.pm_detail`**. All three sampled populations lie
within the "maintained" set — yet none is genetically secure. Range-wide census
(~`{python} R.census_value` mature, EN) nominally clears the $N_c \geq `{python} f"{R.nc_proxy:,.0f}"`$
proxy, but that is the wrong denominator for a
*per-population* indicator: the species is fragmented into subpopulations far below it (e.g. Keo Seima
~`{python} R.cambodia_count`). **Still present ≠ genetically viable** — the gap between the two Goal-A indicators is the
communicable point, and a caution for reporters who might read occupancy-based indicators as
sufficient.

## Wolf: exact reproduction, then the fragility axes

At **GERP > 4 the per-individual realized and masked loads reproduce the deposit's precomputed
`LoadPerInd.thres4` table exactly** — 95th-percentile relative error
`{python} f"{R.anchor_relative_error:.1e}"` and raw count deltas of `{python} R.anchor_deltas` across
all `{python} R.anchor_n` individuals — confirming the re-implementation is faithful before
any extension. The biological signal is recovered correctly: the inbred **Scandinavian** cohorts carry
**realized > masked** load (`{python} f"{R.scandinavian_realized_low:.3f}–{R.scandinavian_realized_high:.3f}"`
realized versus `{python} f"{R.scandinavian_masked_low:.3f}–{R.scandinavian_masked_high:.3f}"` masked),
whereas outbred references (**Finland, Russia, immigrants**) carry **masked > realized**
(`{python} f"{R.outbred_masked_low:.3f}–{R.outbred_masked_high:.3f}"` masked versus
`{python} f"{R.outbred_realized_low:.3f}–{R.outbred_realized_high:.3f}"` realized) — the masked-to-realized
conversion expected when inbreeding exposes recessive load [@smeds2022; @bertorelle2022].

Both knobs move magnitude but not the pattern. Mean realized load falls `{python} R.load_means` across
GERP `{python} R.load_thresholds` (a stricter conservation filter keeps fewer, higher-confidence
sites), and mean $F_{ROH}$ falls `{python} f"{R.roh_mean_low:.3f}"` →
`{python} f"{R.roh_mean_high:.3f}"` as the ROH-length cutoff rises
`{python} f"{R.roh_low_cutoff:g}"` → `{python} f"{R.roh_high_cutoff:g}"` Mb (separating recent long ROH from
ancient background). The realized-versus-masked *direction* is robust to the GERP threshold — the
wolf-side counterpart to the peafowl fragility finding: the number depends on the choice, the signal
does not.

![Cross-chapter fragility scorecard computed from the existing peafowl cube, GBF tables, wolf-load
table, and wolf-ROH table. Categories summarize stability under the settings tested here; they are
not claims of universal robustness beyond these data and methods.](../results/figures/fragility_scorecard.png){#fig-fragility-scorecard
fig-alt="Scorecard classifying project conclusions as robust, magnitude-sensitive, insufficient-evidence, or method-dependent." width="95%"}

# Limitations

We claim **risk, not demonstrated inbreeding depression**. For the peafowl, small per-population $n$
(`{python} R.population_n_compact`) yields wide $N_e$ CIs and many *indeterminate* verdicts by construction; the estimates should
not be cited as point values, and the temporal contrast is geographically narrow and aDNA-sensitive.
Both chapters are **reanalyses of published data**, so the peafowl conclusion ("small, fragmented
populations have small $N_e$") is expected rather than novel, and the wolf load reproduces a published
result. The genuine contribution is methodological: a quantified demonstration that a live policy
indicator (the GBF $N_e > 500$ verdict) and a load estimate are sensitive to defensible analyst
choices, with the two GBF indicators shown to disagree on the same species. GONE2 (borrowed rate) and
the ROH recombination rate (no dense wolf map) are documented approximations. The fragility cube
quantifies, rather than hides, this uncertainty.

# What evidence would change the conclusion?

The limitations above are decision points, not promises to collect more data. This evidence map
identifies the smallest defensible next observation for each unresolved inference; none is required
to reproduce the present analysis.

| Current conclusion | What remains unresolved | Most useful next evidence | How it would change the decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| No sampled peafowl population confidently clears $N_e>500$. | Wide confidence intervals and non-convergence at population sample sizes `{python} R.population_n_compact`. | More independently sampled individuals **per population**. | Narrower intervals could turn an indeterminate cell into pass or fail; until then, retain the three-state verdict. |
| The GONE2 trajectory is consistent with recent decline but is context only. | Peafowl linkage distances are approximated with a borrowed avian recombination rate. | A species-specific recombination map. | It would test the trajectory's timing and scale; it would not replace currentNe2 as the contemporary GBF input. |
| Genomic patterns indicate inbreeding risk, not demonstrated inbreeding depression. | The project has no direct measure of survival, fertility, or reproductive success. | Individual fitness and reproductive measurements linked to genomic inbreeding. | A genotype–fitness association could support a depression claim; load and ROH alone cannot. |
| Populations Maintained is `{python} R.pm_detail` at country resolution. | Country-level presence can hide sub-country loss and fragmentation. | Verified, time-stamped sub-country occurrence or occupancy records. | Finer records would revise the PM denominator/numerator and show whether nominally extant units retain multiple populations. |
| Adding loci alone is unlikely to resolve the peafowl uncertainty. | Millions of SNPs do not create more independent genomes; LD-based uncertainty is dominated by very small individual samples. | Prioritize additional individuals before additional SNP density. | If uncertainty shrinks with more individuals, sampling—not marker count—was limiting; otherwise estimator/model choice needs renewed scrutiny. |

# Reproducibility statement

All analytical results are built by the Snakemake DAG from two public deposits; the Streamlit explorer reads the
outputs only.

The report performs a render-time schema check and reads its headline analytical values from the
following workflow outputs. Missing files or columns stop the render rather than preserving stale
prose.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-report-provenance
#| tbl-cap: "Workflow outputs loaded by the report at render time."
R.provenance
```

```bash
CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64 micromamba create -n congen -f environment.lock.yml  # Apple Silicon/Rosetta
micromamba activate congen && conda config --env --set subdir osx-64
scripts/build_tools.sh                                 # currentNe2 + GONE2, pinned commits
scripts/fetch_data.sh && scripts/extract_data.sh       # Dryad data
snakemake all --cores 4                                # phases 1-5A: analyses, artifacts, and final gates
report/render_report.sh                                # schema-check values and render report/report.html
streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py                     # the live fragility explorer
```

Every threshold and parameter lives in `config/config.yaml`; per-phase gates
(`validate_phase{1..4}`) assert the outputs are well-formed and, for the wolf load, reconcile against
the deposit's own numbers. R packages ship with the conda environment (R is conda-owned; no
`renv.lock`).
